title: Refined Thickness Bounds for High-Index Layers
scientific_hypothesis: Narrowing optimization bounds for HfO2 layers in the 200-240 nm range will reduce overshooting during gradient optimization and improve convergence toward the optimal cavity resonance, yielding higher target scores than route_01's broad 50-250 nm bounds.
design_principle: Admittance locus method with bounded thickness optimization; tight bounds prevent optimizer from exploring non-productive thickness regions identified in route_01 candidates.
proposed_topology: Air | Cr (1 layer) | [HfO2/SiO2] x 8 pairs | Al substrate; total 17 finite layers
design_variables: HfO2 thickness (180-240 nm, narrowed from route_01)
soft_objectives: improve target score over route_01 baseline
manufacturing_considerations: thickness tolerances ±5 nm feasible for sputtering
theory_basis: Admittance locus tracking for layer-by-layer deposition optimization
Gradient-based thickness optimization with bounded search space
expected_advantages: Faster convergence due to reduced search space
Avoids overshooting optimal resonance identified in route_01 candidates
known_risks: Bounds may be too restrictive if optimal thickness lies outside 180-240 nm range
May not escape local optimum from route_01
execution_request_english: Optimize a 17-layer stack on Al substrate: Layer 1 is Cr (50-100 nm), Layers 2-17 are 8 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs. HfO2 layers (even indices 2,4,6,8,10,12,14,16) bounded 180-240 nm. SiO2 layers (odd indices 3,5,7,9,11,13,15,17) bounded 100-200 nm. Use gradient_thickness optimizer with reduced adaptive step size for HfO2 layers. Evaluate at normal incidence, unpolarized, 400-2000 nm spectrum. Score: weighted absorptance in 400-700 nm plus weighted reflectance in 700-2000 nm. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 400-700 nm, 700-2000 nm. soft objectives: high absorptance in 400-700 nm; low reflectance in 400-700 nm; high reflectance in 700-2000 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: high reflectance in 400-700 nm; high absorptance in 700-2000 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count not exceeding 20.
revision_reason: Narrowed HfO2 thickness bounds from 50-250 nm to 180-240 nm based on route_01 candidate analysis showing optimal layers cluster in 200-240 nm range; reduced step size to prevent overshooting
